<subject>NAAG</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association of Agricultural Regulators ("NAAR") regarding their involvement on the agribusiness side, specifically with regard to Section 12(A) clearances.

According to Tripti, there is no group effort that exists (i.e., an agribusiness committee or an individual regulator taking the lead on commodity trading issues).  Individual regulators get involved, but that is all.  For example, Kisan Producers Association recently opposed Green Earth Commodities' application for 12(A) clearance, but the Agricultural Ministry still granted Green Earth's petition.

Tripti recommends that we use the regulators as much as possible.  For example, if we believe that local market competition is non-existent and we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to the individual regulator and have him/her weigh in on our behalf.  Tripti recognizes that AgriIndia is pro-competitive and that typically the regulators would be in agreement with our positions - so it's something for us to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that the Agricultural Ministry will listen to the regulators, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know.  Thanks.

Hiral Acharya, Director
AgriIndia Pvt. Ltd.

Pune, Maharashtra 411001
